epigraph.quote: When a conglomerate splits into focused pieces, the market's first instinct is confusion; the disciplined investor's edge is separating the permanent earnings power from the departed division—and waiting for the tape to settle.
epigraph.author: Executive Investment Desk Note

web_blocks.html: India Glycols Limited (NSE: INDIAGLYCO) has just completed one of the cleanest structural resets in Indian mid-cap chemicals. Yet both its headline valuation ratios and its near-term stock chart are sending misleading signals to casual observers [1][2]. Under the NCLT-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement (Appointed Date April 1, 2026; Effective Date September 1, 2026), INDIAGLYCO carved out two major divisions. It separated its high-margin Potable Spirits & Bio-Fuels business (IGL Spirits Ltd) and its Nutraceuticals unit (Ennature Bio Pharma Ltd). The listed entity now operates as a focused Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC) and Industrial Gases platform alongside a 49% equity stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals [2][3][8][11].

That boundary reset halved consolidated borrowings from ₹1,691 Cr (March 2026) to ₹826 Cr (September 2026). It also slashed quarterly interest expense from ₹45–49 Cr to ₹12 Cr [1][7]. At the same time, the split removed ~66% of revenue and the ~21% EBIT-margin liquor engine. Continuing operations printed ₹357 Cr (Q1 FY27) and ₹362 Cr (Q2 FY27), an annualized run-rate of ₹1,438 Cr revenue, 11.0% OPM, and ~₹114 Cr headline continuing PAT (₹97.5 Cr at a normalized 25% tax rate) [1][4]. Consequently, Screener's headline 9.27x P/E (6.0x on TradingView, reflecting the post-cutoff 2026-11-16 quote of ₹292.45) is an accounting mirage. At the 2026-11-13 ledger close of ₹311.30 (MCap ₹2,086 Cr on 6.70 Cr shares), INDIAGLYCO trades at 18.5x headline continuing P/E (21.4x tax-normalized) and 14.2x–16.0x EV/EBITDA (ex-investments), squarely in line with Indian chemical peers [1][24][26].

book_paragraphs: This dossier examines India Glycols Limited at a pivotal inflection point. On September 1, 2026, the company's landmark three-way demerger became effective, separating its Potable Spirits and Ennature Biopharma divisions into standalone entities and leaving the listed company as a pure-play Bio-based Specialties and Performance Chemicals and Industrial Gases platform backed by a 49% joint venture with Clariant.

At first glance, the numbers look contradictory: Q1 and Q2 FY27 revenue dropped 66% to 67% year-on-year to ₹357 crore and ₹362 crore, while Screener displays a tempting 9.27x trailing P/E. Our forensic work proves both are optical illusions of the demerger boundary. On true continuing operations—₹1,438 crore annualized revenue, 11% operating margins, and ₹114 crore of headline net profit (₹97.5 crore at a normalized 25% tax rate)—the stock at the November 13, 2026 ledger close of ₹311.30 (₹2,086 crore market cap) trades at 18.5x headline continuing earnings and 21.4x tax-normalized earnings, fairly valued alongside specialty chemical peers.

Our dual verdict is therefore clear and disciplined. For existing holdings, INDIAGLYCO is NOT_HELD with zero shares in our Zerodha account. For new capital, the verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT under Tactical Momentum at Tier 2 conviction. At the November 13 close of ₹311.30, buying offers an inadequate 0.64:1 reward-to-risk ratio against our ₹243.25 stop (and even the post-cutoff November 16 TradingView quote of ₹292.45, down 6.06%, offers only 1.27:1 in a Stage 3 pullback). Waiting for a confirmed 4-hour reversal inside the ₹269.72–₹277.94 support shelf transforms the setup into an asymmetric 2.22:1 opportunity toward our ₹355 base-case target.

book_subsections.title: Why This Monograph Matters for Special-Situations Investing
paragraphs: Corporate demergers are among the richest hunting grounds in Indian equities, precisely because standard financial data feeds take several quarters to catch up with the new corporate boundary. When India Glycols Limited split off its Potable Spirits and Ennature Biopharma divisions effective September 1, 2026, it created a classic analytical puzzle: a headline 66% to 67% year-on-year revenue drop in Q1 and Q2 FY27 paired with a seemingly mouth-watering 9.27x trailing P/E on Screener.

Throughout the ten chapters of this monograph, you and I have stripped away both illusions. We traced the Kashipur bio-MEG and bio-EO plant's forty-year evolution, separated the continuing Bio-based Specialties and Performance Chemicals and Industrial Gases engines from the departed liquor division, audited the ₹826 crore post-demerger debt load and ₹422 crore Clariant JV investment, and benchmarked the true 18.5x headline (21.4x tax-normalized) continuing P/E against Galaxy Surfactants, Rossari Biotech, IG Petrochemicals, and Balaji Amines.

The result is an honest, unhedged conclusion: INDIAGLYCO is a credible CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL green-chemistry platform, not a high-ROE compounder, and it is currently digesting a Stage 3 consolidation at ₹311.30 (with a post-cutoff November 16 quote at ₹292.45). By refusing to chase current prices and waiting for a confirmed 4-hour turn inside the ₹269.72–₹277.94 support zone against a ₹243.25 stop, we let both valuation and the tape work in our favor.

book_subsections.title: Chapter-by-Chapter Roadmap of the Underwriting
paragraphs: In Chapters 1 through 3, we examine India Glycols Limited's forty-year corporate evolution from its 1983 founding in Kashipur through its 2021 Clariant joint venture carve-out, its ₹467 crore November 2025 preferential deleveraging, and the September 1, 2026 three-way demerger. We break down the continuing Bio-based Specialties and Performance Chemicals division, the Industrial Gases segment, and the unit economics of molasses- and grain-route bio-MEG versus crude-linked petrochemical MEG.

In Chapters 4 through 6, we test the competitive moat against global bio-fermentation peers like Corbion and historical base-rate failures like Amyris, audit management's capital-allocation track record, and forensically reconstruct the 10-year financial history—highlighting why 3-year ROE averaged 10.4%, why Free Cash Flow remained negative across FY22–FY26, and how the September 2026 balance sheet reset halved borrowings to ₹826 crore.

Finally, in Chapters 7 through 9, we dismantle Screener's 9.27x pre-demerger P/E illusion, run a Reverse DCF and peer comparison against Galaxy Surfactants, Rossari Biotech, IG Petrochemicals, and Balaji Amines, map the Stage 3 technical structure and ₹269.72–₹277.94 support shelf, and lay out our exact WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT cash-equity execution plan.

book_subsections.title: What to Watch in Q3 and Q4 FY27
paragraphs: As India Glycols Limited reports its next two quarters as a standalone green-chemicals and industrial-gases company, your attention should stay laser-focused on three numbers: continuing operating margin moving above 12% from the current 11.0% baseline, quarterly interest expense holding steady at or below ₹12 crore, and consistent dividend or profit upstreaming from the 49% Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals joint venture.

On the price chart, watch the ₹269.72–₹277.94 support zone around Pivot S1 (₹273.83) and the rising 30-week simple moving average at ₹253.05. If the stock holds that shelf, prints a confirmed four-hour reversal on expanding volume, and turns up toward ₹305, the 2.22:1 asymmetry to our ₹355 base target becomes actionable for a 3% to 5% Tier 2 cash-equity starter. If it closes below ₹243.25, walk away without hesitation.

book_subsections.title: Executive Numbers at a Glance
paragraphs: To keep the key anchors top of mind as you listen through the chapters ahead: the November 13, 2026 ledger close is ₹311.30 (with a separate post-cutoff November 16 TradingView quote of ₹292.45, down 6.06%); market capitalization on 6.70 crore shares is ₹2,086 crore; post-demerger continuing revenue is running at ₹1,438 crore annualized with 11.0% operating margins, ₹114 crore of headline continuing net profit, and ₹97.5 crore on a normalized 25% tax rate, putting continuing P/E at 18.5x headline and 21.4x tax-normalized rather than Screener's 9.27x; September 2026 borrowings stand at ₹826 crore against ₹422 crore of investments; our support buy zone is ₹269.72 to ₹277.94; our hard invalidation stop is ₹243.25; and our twelve-to-eighteen-month scenario targets are ₹211 bear, ₹355 base, and ₹420 bull, with zero shares currently held in Zerodha.

Remember also our core portfolio discipline: in a narrow-breadth Nifty 50 uptrend, patience is a competitive edge. We have no reason to chase a Stage 3 chemical stock when waiting for ₹269.72–₹277.94 turns a sub-par 0.64:1 trade at ₹311.30 (or 1.27:1 at the post-cutoff ₹292.45 quote) into a crisp 2.22:1 asymmetric entry. Keep your marginal cash ready, set the alert at ₹277.94, demand a four-hour reversal confirmation, and let the numbers—never the headline P/E—guide your capital. With that discipline locked in, let us walk through India Glycols Limited's story from its 1983 Kashipur origins to today's post-demerger inflection.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Discipline Over Headline Noise
book_callouts.text: Post-demerger stocks reward investors who do two things well: rebuild the continuing P&L from scratch instead of trusting stale trailing multiples, and let the chart finish its digestion before stepping in. With ₹826 crore of debt—half its March 2026 level—and a unique green-chemistry footprint, INDIAGLYCO earns a spot on our active watch list, provided we let price come to ₹269.72–₹277.94 first.
